# @arki/expr

> A safe expression language for user-typed formulas: a parser, a typed AST, canonical printing, and evaluation in float, decimal, rational and complex domains. It is not a computer algebra system and not a scripting language.

Never store the user's raw text. Store `print(parse(text))`, and treat every stored AST as untrusted.

## Import paths

<!-- llms:start -->
- `@arki/expr`: a safe expression language on `@arki/math`. `ExprLimitError`, `ParseError`, `canonical`, `children`, `decimalComma`, `defineLanguage`, `defineSyntax`, `fromJSON`, `names`, `parse`, `parseEquation`, `print`; and 34 more.
- `@arki/expr/float`: the float domain (RFC §8, §10). `compile`, `compileEquation`, `evaluate`; types `AbortSignalLike`, `Angle`, `CompileOptions`, `CompiledEquation`, `CompiledFunction`, `EvaluateOptions`, `FloatFunction`, `HostImplementations`, `Reading`; and 2 more.
- `@arki/expr/latex`: LaTeX for display (RFC §12, C-26). `toLatex`; types `LatexOptions`.
- `@arki/expr/decimal`: the Decimal domain (RFC §8). `Decimal`, `compile`, `compileEquation`, `evaluate`; types `AbortSignalLike`, `CallOptions`, `CompileOptions`, `CompiledEquation`, `CompiledFunction`, `DecimalContext`, `DecimalFunction`, `DecimalInput`; and 6 more.
- `@arki/expr/rational`: the Rational domain (RFC §8). `Rational`, `compile`, `compileEquation`, `evaluate`; types `AbortSignalLike`, `CallOptions`, `CompileOptions`, `CompiledEquation`, `CompiledFunction`, `Detailed`, `EvaluateOptions`, `ExactLimits`; and 4 more.
- `@arki/expr/complex`: the Complex domain (RFC §8). `Complex`, `compile`, `compileEquation`, `evaluate`; types `AbortSignalLike`, `Angle`, `CallOptions`, `CompileOptions`, `CompiledEquation`, `CompiledFunction`, `ComplexFunction`, `ComplexLike`; and 5 more.
<!-- llms:end -->

## Rules that bite

- Only `f.sample` returns `NaN`. Every other failure throws.
- The Decimal domain throws `RoundingNecessaryError` until you pass a rounding mode.
- No domain falls back to float; a missing function is `not-in-domain`.
- Every input has a budget; going over throws `ExprLimitError`.
